gaps.note: All 21 networks, lever P6. The unit theme-claim-operators wrote no research file, so the question whether an ordinary account can move other users' ERC-6909 claims through a contract they approved has no answer on any network. Its work directory holds most of the data: raw/logs_*.json (OperatorSet and Approval logs), raw/exposure_*.json for 15 networks, raw/guard_*.json (probe of each operator contract), raw/posm_actions.json and three exit simulations. The exposure files list 200 operator or spender addresses on Base whose approving owners hold claims of about 407,567 USD in the large tokens, 227 on Ethereum with about 79,819 USD and 143 on Robinhood Chain with about 16,103 USD. These sums may count an owner once per operator and nobody checked them. The scans for BNB Smart Chain (17,870 log windows) and X Layer were still running when the unit stopped, and exposure files for chain ids 56, 196, 1868, 7777777, 4326 and 4217 do not exist. The second half of the task has results that are in no state file: posm_actions.json shows that the PositionManager has 23,877 bytes on 19 networks and 19,965 bytes on Elysium and HyperEVM, handles the same action numbers on all 21 and refuses action 23 (MINT_6909), and raw/exit_42220_178.json and raw/exit_137_60652.json show that with one currency refusing transfers every sequence that pays or closes the blocked side reverts, MINT_6909 reverts with 0x5cda29d7 and argument 0x17, and the only sequences that succeed give the blocked side up (clear or take with the maximum set to uint256 max) or put the blocked delta into a new one sided position.

All 21 networks. Only theme-shared-hooks has a verdict file. The eleven findings of established-l1 (3), theme-assigned-balance (5) and theme-unbacked-claims (3) and every cleared item of those units and of op-stack-eth were checked by nobody. Two of the unverified findings are proposed as high with actor unprivileged (QANX and the generator tokens, and the revocable grants of ADX and CDT). Under SCHEMA.md a finding is confirmed only after a second agent checked the chain fact and the code path, so none of the eleven should be merged as confirmed.

All 21 networks. No unit has read src/ since cycle 3. The plan of cycle 5 ran four themes in the code slots, and the high leads L-313, L-314 and L-260 and the leads L-204, L-232 and L-016 were assigned to nobody for the second cycle in a row. Critic check on 2026-11-23, read only: I placed a stub at the fee controller address by state override on Ethereum, Polygon and Arc (eth_call on the endpoints of state/networks.json). The stub calls unlock and, inside unlockCallback, calls collectProtocolFees(stub, 0x00000000000000000000000000000000deadbeef, 0). The call returned success with 32 bytes of return data on all three, and the same call sent directly from the controller address while the manager is locked also returned zero without reverting. The deployed PoolManagers therefore collect fees inside an unlock, as src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57 reads. The cycle 1 cleared items for chain ids 1, 137, 56 and 5042 already walked that case for a gain and found none, so the first of the four places that L-313 lists is answered. The other three (sync without a lock, take on an address without code, and unlock, take, settle, settleFor, mint and burn without noDelegateCall) were not walked against network features by any unit, and I did not test them.

Monad, World Chain, Celo and Avalanche. Critic check on 2026-11-23, read only: one eth_simulateV1 request with two calls in one simulated block to a contract placed by state override. The first call runs TSTORE(0, 1) and the second returns TLOAD(0). The second call returned zero on 17 networks: on the endpoints of state/networks.json for chain ids 1, 10, 8453, 130, 7777777, 57073, 1868, 42161, 4663, 99901, 137, 56 and 4217, on arc.drpc.org for Arc, on rpc.purroofgroup.com and hyperliquid.drpc.org for HyperEVM, on xlayer.drpc.org for X Layer and on megaeth.drpc.org for MegaETH. The endpoints I tried for Monad (rpc.monad.xyz, rpc2.monad.xyz, monad.drpc.org), World Chain, Celo (forno.celo.org, celo.drpc.org) and Avalanche refused the method or failed. For these four networks assumption A1 rests on source readings alone. The test exercises the simulation path of an RPC node. It says nothing about block production on HyperEVM and MegaETH, where the producing node or the payload builder is closed, and the HyperEVM endpoints run third party clients.

Base, BNB Smart Chain, World Chain and X Layer. Two units of this cycle say that the Initialize history of these PoolManagers cannot be read from public endpoints (established-l1 for BNB Smart Chain, op-stack-eth for Base and World Chain), while theme-shared-hooks read it in the same cycle: 341,033 Initialize logs on BNB Smart Chain from block 45,970,610 through a NodeReal endpoint, 15,572,154 pools on Base through base.gateway.tenderly.co (one window in four between blocks 37,000,001 and 49,000,000), 4,758 pools on World Chain through a QuickNode endpoint and 2,833 pools on X Layer for the last 1.4 million blocks. The token tests of this cycle ran on much smaller lists: theme-assigned-balance tested 9,108 currencies on Base, 3,369 on BNB Smart Chain, 851 on World Chain and 96 on X Layer, the trigger probe of op-stack-eth used the same Base list (tokens that moved in one day), and the shared balance test of established-l1 covered 1,364 currencies from 31 hours of pool creation on BNB Smart Chain. A pooled token on these four networks that did not move in the sampled day has never been tested for a lock, a clawback, an idle sweep or a second address. Leads L-317 and L-291 came back inconclusive for this reason.

Robinhood Chain, Elysium and Arc hold 1.13 million of the 1.24 million pooled currencies. theme-assigned-balance covered them through families and samples: on Robinhood Chain one token per code hash for hashes shared by more than three tokens and three tokens per code size for the rest, and the unit's own lead says the full balance transfer test did not finish on the three networks. Function names came from a signature database that knew 85,092 of 137,912 selectors, so 52,820 selectors were never tried. Tokens that run as precompiles (TIP-20, B20) were covered by one transfer test and by documentation. The cleared item that lists tokens refusing a full transfer from the PoolManager records counts per network (Optimism 110, Arbitrum One 178, Polygon 104, Monad 62, World Chain 43, Ink 39, Unichain 37, Base 27, BNB Smart Chain 21, Avalanche 20, Robinhood Chain 2,439, Arc 115) and looked at the cause only for six Ethereum tokens priced above 100,000 USD. The other refusals are neither valued nor classed, so that item is a list of open cases and should not be filed as cleared.

Hook census. theme-shared-hooks ranked hooks by pools per address and probed 111 hooks on 21 networks. On Arc 206,554 pools name a hook and 194,252 distinct hook addresses appear, and the most used address serves 2,003 pools, so more than nine tenths of the hooked pools on Arc sit behind addresses that were not read and that probably share a few code templates. The census did not group by code hash on any network. It did not rank hooks by what they hold, and the one finding (Klik) came from a hook family with small claim balances. On Base one window in four was read for 12 million blocks and three sample pools per hook were kept. On X Layer 1.4 million blocks were read. The probes called callbacks outside an unlock, so every path ends at ManagerLocked on the first take, mint or burn and later steps were not observed. Several top hooks have no verified source (for example 0x6b1216a40b65c83e9c9e18a562c446697b8cf8ec with 104,615 pools on Elysium and 0xf0e1b03731fa1c94b30e90a9a61368e2f5968088 on Optimism) and were judged from revert selectors.

Ethereum, Celo, X Layer, Monad and MegaETH. The sixteen shape sweep through a forwarding stub at the PoolManager address (empty calldata with and without value, transfer with 0 and 1, balanceOf, the ten hook selectors, unlockCallback) has now run on Tempo, Arc and HyperEVM (cycle 4), on Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche and the seven OP Stack chains with ETH gas (cycle 5), and in an earlier form on the three Nitro chains (cycle 3). These five networks have only the four shape test of lead L-166. Lead L-209 stays open for them.

OP Mainnet and Unichain. The Lagoon clearances rest on source from the develop branch and from op-contracts v4.0.0. Slots 0x22 to 0x28 and 0x30 hold no implementation on any chain today, the activation timestamps are not set, and the notice gives 10 December 2026 for the two Sepolia chains and 11 January 2027 for mainnet pending a vote. The OP Mainnet sequencer still reports a build without a version, so the client reading for that chain is of two releases that follow it. The unit states that after Lagoon any account can make 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000023 the msg.sender of a call to the PoolManager. No unit asked which ERC-6909 balances, operator rights or positions exist under addresses that execute calls for any caller, on any network.

Polygon, BNB Smart Chain and Avalanche. Three statements of established-l1 leave the upgrade lens thin. Polygon distributed Uburu, the security release v2.11.1 and Purley as private builds and published the source at or after activation, and Uburu replaced the code at 0x1001, so the next change to 0x1010 cannot be read in advance and the probe of F-008 must be repeated after every Bor release. On BNB Smart Chain Jenner activates on 2026-12-08: the CAS20 behaviour was observed on the Chapel testnet with 12 tokens, mainnet token creation stays closed until an administrator acts, the package paymentlanemeta was not read, and the v1.7 source with the fused opcodes was not read. On Avalanche the Igloo rule set for the C-Chain is unpublished. Cells for lenses L5 and L6 are still at depth 2 from cycle 1 on all 21 networks.

Eleven networks in six families. The two angles of this cycle (upcoming forks, and one balance under two currency ids) ran for established-l1 and op-stack-eth only. Ethereum was last visited in cycle 2 although six findings of this cycle name chain id 1, and no unit has asked which Ethereum fork is scheduled. The equal balance grouping that found the two EURe addresses is complete on Polygon and Avalanche, partial on BNB Smart Chain, and was not run on the other networks. Critic check on 2026-11-23, read only: ArbOwnerPublic.getScheduledUpgrade() (selector 0x81ef944c at 0x6b) returns two zero words on Elysium, Robinhood Chain and Arbitrum One, and ArbSys.arbOSVersion() returns 0x74 on all three. No ArbOS upgrade is scheduled on Elysium today, so leads L-001 and L-134 still cannot be answered.

theme-unbacked-claims. The mechanism text of its second finding (token contracts that burned or moved the PoolManager balance) contains eleven unfilled placeholders (%s) where the counts for Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain belong, so the size of the result on those two networks is not in the file. The search for balance falls sees transfers to burn addresses only. A token that lets a third party move the PoolManager balance to an ordinary address is visible only in census windows of 0.5 days on Base, 2 days on World Chain, 3 days on Ethereum and up to 30 days elsewhere. The burn search covers recent windows on Base, World Chain and Robinhood Chain and 400,000 blocks on X Layer. Base and Robinhood Chain hold 39.6 of the 53.3 million claim mints and were sampled with a lighter rule. Part (c) of lead L-318, native takes to a recipient other than the caller, was not done. The Pleasing USD finding rests on two revert texts and the implementation behind the proxy was not read.

Tempo and Elysium. protocolFeeController is the zero address on both (state/networks.json). The question whether any transaction type, system call or precompile can call a contract with msg.sender equal to address(0) has a cleared item for Avalanche, Celo, X Layer, the five OP Stack chains without a controller, Monad, MegaETH and HyperEVM. I found no such item for Tempo or Elysium in state/cleared.json. The checks at src/ProtocolFees.sol:36 and 48 compare msg.sender with that stored value and nothing else.

Carried over without work. The Celo half of lead L-218 (the PositionManager and the first Universal Router return the CELO token, which is the native balance, as their wrapped native address) is unanswered for the fifth cycle. F-024 on X Layer stays plausible on one fact and lead L-263, which names the observation that would settle it, was not taken. The behaviour test of the Unichain predeploy (lead L-217) was not run. Lead L-315 about the rule by which the Robinhood Chain filter gains entries has been open at high priority since cycle 4 and its parent L-117 since cycle 1, and no unit has read the filter contract or its logs.

leads.question: Finish the first half of theme-claim-operators from the files in research/network-risk/cycles/005/theme-claim-operators.work/raw. For every contract that still is an operator or holds an allowance from an owner with a claim balance above zero, read its code: can any caller make it call PoolManager.transferFrom(sender, receiver, id, amount) or PoolManager.burn(from, id, amount) with a sender the caller chooses? Start with the 200 addresses in exposure_8453.json (about 407,567 USD of claims in large tokens), the 227 in exposure_1.json and the 143 in exposure_4663.json, then complete the log scans for chain ids 56 and 196 and build the exposure files for the six networks that have none.
leads.why: transferFrom and burn accept an operator or an allowance without any other check (src/ERC6909.sol:35-48, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22, src/PoolManager.sol:332-336). An approved contract that forwards calls for anyone lets an ordinary account burn those claims inside its own unlock and take the tokens. This is the one lever of the list P1 to P8 with no result in five cycles.

leads.question: Rank hooks by what they hold. For each network take the 20 hook addresses with the largest ERC-6909 claim balances (from the claim mint logs that theme-unbacked-claims collected, then balanceOf(hook, id)) and the largest token and native balances, and on Arc first group the 194,252 hook addresses by code hash and take the ten largest groups. For each: is the ledger that decides a payout stored under the pool id, and can an ordinary account initialize a pool that names this hook, or reach its callbacks through a public factory? Run the callbacks inside an unlock with eth_simulateV1 or debug_traceCall so that the calls after the first take or burn are visible.
leads.why: The Klik finding shows the fault: a ledger per token that is paid in the currency of the calling pool. It was found among the most used hooks, and it holds tens of dollars. A hook with the same fault and large claims would let an account that opens its own pool take what the hook holds for other pools. No unit ranked hooks by value, and more than nine tenths of the hooked pools on Arc use addresses nobody read.

leads.question: Build the full currency list of the PoolManager on Base, BNB Smart Chain and World Chain with the log sources theme-shared-hooks used in cycle 5 (base.gateway.tenderly.co in windows of 1,000 blocks, the NodeReal endpoint for BNB Smart Chain, the QuickNode endpoint for World Chain), and on X Layer as far back as the endpoint serves. Rerun xfer_sweep.py, assign_sweep.py and third_sweep.py from theme-assigned-balance.work and the equal balance grouping of established-l1 on the new lists. Which tokens with a price let a third party lock, claw back, sweep or mirror the PoolManager balance?
leads.why: The tested lists hold 9,108 currencies on Base against 15.6 million pools, 3,369 on BNB Smart Chain against 341,033 pools, 851 on World Chain and 96 on X Layer. Base carries the most value after Ethereum, and DEAD, the one token an ordinary account has already emptied, is on Base. This closes L-317 and L-291.

leads.question: For every pooled token with a price and a PoolManager balance above 1,000 USD: call, from an unrelated address, each function of the token and of the contracts its balanceOf reads that takes an address argument, with the PoolManager as that argument, and record whether balanceOf(PoolManager) falls and who receives the amount. Run each trial twice, at the current block and with the block time overridden by 400 days and by 8 hours (eth_call block override), so that inactivity sweeps, expiries and rebases that are not yet due show up. Include the 52,820 selectors the signature database could not name.
leads.why: claimIdleTokens of DeadToken on Base moved the whole pooled balance to an ordinary account after 90 quiet days, and the search found it only because part of the amount is burned. A test at the current time cannot see a rule that waits for a date. A priced token with such a rule is a loss for hookless pools that an ordinary account can cause.

leads.question: Answer leads L-117 and L-315 from chain data on Robinhood Chain. Read the filter contract and the logs of the filterer account: what does each of the entries identify (a transaction hash, a sender, a contract, any address touched during execution), which account adds them and how soon after the transaction they follow, and do the listed transactions share a touched address? Then test by eth_call and debug_traceCall whether a transaction that calls 0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951 touches a listed address when a pool it uses was sent 1 wei, or a zero amount native take, from or to that address by someone else.
leads.why: F-001 records that the filter can fail any exit, including forced ones. If entries follow a rule on touched addresses and the rule can be met by state that an ordinary account leaves in the PoolManager or in a pooled token, that account can make other users' withdrawals fail. Robinhood Chain has 1.17 million pools and no unit has read the filter in five cycles.

leads.question: Verify the two unverified high findings of theme-assigned-balance in one sitting. Through a stub at the PoolManager address (state override, one eth_call or eth_simulateV1 per token) replay: take X, sync, transferLocked on QANX 0xaaa7a10a8ee237ea61e8ac46c50a8db8bcc1baaa or freezeTo on one generator token per network, settle, then a transfer of the full balance. For ADX 0x4470bb87d77b963a013db939be332f927f2b992e and CDT 0x177d39ac676ed1c67a2b268ad7f1e58826e5b0af replay take, sync, grantVestedTokens with revokable set, settle, revokeTokenGrant, and compare balanceOf(PoolManager) with the value before the take. Then search the selector families of theme-assigned-balance.work for transferLocked, freezeTo, grantVestedTokens and revokeTokenGrant on tokens with a pooled value above 1,000 USD on all 21 networks.
leads.why: These are the only findings of the cycle proposed as high with actor unprivileged, and no second agent has checked them. The amounts found are close to nothing, so the severity depends on whether a priced token of the same design is pooled anywhere.

leads.question: Write up the second half of theme-claim-operators from raw/posm_actions.json and the three raw/exit_*.json files, and repeat the exit simulation on one more network with a token that refuses transfers from the PoolManager (a paused wrapped stock token on Monad or a frozen TIP-20 on Tempo). Which action sequence of the PositionManager lets a liquidity provider leave with the other currency, what happens to the blocked side in each (given up through clear, or kept as a one sided position), and can the official front end produce that sequence?
leads.why: The simulations on Celo and Polygon show that MINT_6909 is refused and that the working exits give the blocked side up or leave it in a position. If the interface offers neither, a block on one token by its issuer or by a quota that an ordinary account can use up (F-072) freezes the other currency of those positions as well.

leads.question: Which ModifyLiquidity logs of each PoolManager name as sender, and which ERC-6909 balances name as owner, an address that executes calls for any caller: Multicall3 0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11, the Across MulticallHandler, the settlement and relay contracts that the cycle 4 shared transaction unit listed, and EIP-7702 accounts whose delegate has a batch function without a caller check? For each hit, is liquidity or a claim balance still there?
leads.why: Positions belong to msg.sender of modifyLiquidity and claims to the address named in mint (src/PoolManager.sol:161 and 322-336). Anything held under an address that forwards calls can be removed by any account inside its own unlock. After Lagoon the messenger 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000023 on OP Mainnet and Unichain becomes such an address. No unit has listed these owners.

leads.question: Run the equal balance grouping of established-l1 (balanceOf(PoolManager) for every pooled currency, groups of identical non zero balances, one unit transfer per member) on Ethereum, OP Mainnet, Base, Unichain, Arbitrum One, Monad and HyperEVM. On Ethereum start with the two EURe addresses 0x3231Cb76718CDeF2155FC47b5286d82e6eDA273f and 0x39b8B6385416f4cA36a20319F70D28621895279D and the other Monerium tokens: which pools use each address and how much is owed under each id?
leads.why: The test found a second working address for EURe on Polygon and is complete on two networks only. Ethereum holds 4,188.47 EURe readable at both addresses. Core conserves value per id, so the hazard found so far is an issuer freeze, and a pair in which one address reports in another unit has not been ruled out beyond the 170 most pooled tokens.

leads.question: In the Klik factories (0x20839c453a0ed8bcab1095ea068669469098297c on Tempo, 0xb6da931df2ed2c80db47923d4eb46fd913ee01c3 and 0x95e0da371711502eed78bcc3f17856b4415120ca on Ethereum, and factory() of each other hook): may any account call the launch function, and does collectFees(token) pay creatorFees[token] in pairOf(token) whatever currency the hook credited? Did the launcher of 0xfd23280b87514ce09dcb47965f1c5465847422eb withdraw the 34130246063283906 SPCXon credited in Ethereum transaction 0xd903d0ada1874646896a5191a2ef25accec3c3db1333914542b6ad9a8c96bfed?
leads.why: The verifier showed that the payout step has run on Ethereum and froze three pools with liquidity. If the factory pays the creator share in the real quote currency, an ordinary launcher turns fees booked in a worthless currency into the factory's balance, which is a direct gain. The amounts today are tens of dollars.

leads.question: Who owns the liquidity positions of the Klik launch pools, can the owner remove them, how much quote currency do these pools hold on the nine networks, and does the sequence the verifier described (initialize a second pool of token T, mint claims of an own currency to the hook, swap there) stop swaps in the real pool of T when run end to end in eth_simulateV1?
leads.why: The verifier derived that any account can stop swaps in the pool of another creator's token and did not simulate it. If the positions are locked in the factory, the quote currency paid by buyers stays in the PoolManager with no swap path, and the severity should follow that amount.

leads.question: For the tokens that refuse a transfer of the full PoolManager balance on OP Mainnet (110), Arbitrum One (178), Polygon (104), Monad (62), World Chain (43), Ink (39), Unichain (37) and Base (27), and for yUSD, yETH and xSolvBTC on Ethereum: which have a price, what is the balance worth, since which block does the refusal hold, and is the cause an entry for the PoolManager address, a rule for all contracts, a pause, or a rule the token's author wrote?
leads.why: About 1.67 million USD is blocked on Ethereum by five tokens, and the other networks were counted and not valued. Whether issuers list the singleton address on purpose decides if the same will happen to a new deployment. The answer also gives the single record of live blocks that two critics have asked for.

leads.question: Run the sixteen shape sweep through a forwarding stub at the PoolManager address on Ethereum, Celo, X Layer, Monad and MegaETH, with the target lists of the earlier top level sweeps. Does any target answer differently from the top level call, return 32 bytes that start with a hook selector, or return a 32 byte true to transfer without being a token?
leads.why: This is what remains of lead L-209. Thirteen networks showed no difference. Celo and X Layer have a non ETH gas token with core contracts of their own, and Monad and MegaETH have precompiles that read the caller's position in the call stack.

leads.question: Test assumption A1 on block production with chain data. On each of these networks find a block in which one transaction calls sync with a token address and no settle follows in that transaction, and a later transaction of the same block calls settle or settleFor with msg.value above zero without a sync of its own. Did the later one succeed? Where an endpoint serves eth_simulateV1 or debug_traceCallMany for Monad, World Chain, Celo or Avalanche, also run the two call TSTORE and TLOAD test of the cycle 5 critic.
leads.why: A native settle reverts with NonzeroNativeValue while a token is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:356), so one such pair in a block shows that the synced currency was cleared between transactions by the node that produced the block. Four endpoints refused the simulation, and the producing nodes of HyperEVM and MegaETH are closed.

leads.question: On Tempo and Elysium, can any transaction type, system transaction, precompile or parent chain message call a contract of the sender's choice with msg.sender equal to address(0)? For Tempo read which sender the end of block system transactions and the fee manager calls carry and whether their target is fixed. For Elysium read how messages from the parent chain are aliased and whether a parent chain sender can map to address(0).
leads.why: protocolFeeController is address(0) on both networks. A caller with that address passes src/ProtocolFees.sol:36 and 48, can set the protocol fee of every pool to the cap and collect it to any recipient. The other eleven networks without a controller have a cleared item for this question.

leads.question: After Lagoon activates on OP Sepolia and Unichain Sepolia (target 10 December 2026): which implementations sit behind 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000022 to 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000028, do ETHLiquidity, SuperchainETHBridge and SuperchainTokenBridge have a receive or fallback function or any selector the PoolManager can send, and what does each return to the sixteen call shapes?
leads.why: The clearance was read from the develop branch because nothing is deployed. A payable fallback would add a recipient that strands a caller's payout (the shape of F-048), which is a loss for the caller only, so this is a check of a clearance and no path to pool funds is known.

leads.question: Before 2026-12-08: has any pool of the BNB Smart Chain PoolManager been initialized with a currency or hook that starts with 0xCA52 or equals 0x70, 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000002007, 0xCA5F000000000000000000000000000000000000 or one of the two 0x7020 registry addresses (filter the full Initialize logs through the endpoint the hooks unit used)? After the fork: which CAS20 tokens exist on mainnet, which have pools, and what do their policy ids, pause bits and role holders say?
leads.why: Jenner turns these addresses from accounts without code into native code fifteen days from now. The unit showed that no credit can exist under them today, and a look at the logs confirms that no pool waits there. F-007 becomes live when the first CAS20 token is pooled.

leads.question: Run the upcoming forks angle on the six families that did not get it in cycle 5. For each network: which upgrade is scheduled or announced for the next six months, and does it add a transaction type, a precompile, a predeploy or a token standard that answers transfer, balanceOf, a hook selector or a value call from the PoolManager? For the clients built on go-ethereum, name the fork at which a call from 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe carries its stated value without a balance transfer (the rule F-058 records on BNB Smart Chain and the cycle 3 reading found switched off on the Nitro chains until Amsterdam rules), and say whether any call from that address can reach a target that an ordinary account chooses.
leads.why: settle credits msg.value without reading a balance (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). A system caller whose value is reported and not moved is harmless only while every call from it has a fixed target and zero value. That was checked for BNB Smart Chain and nowhere else as a question about the future.

leads.question: Answer the Celo half of lead L-218 from the deployed PositionManager and the first Universal Router: which address do they return as wrapped native, what do the WRAP and UNWRAP actions (21 and 22 in posm_actions.json) do when that address is the CELO token, and how do SWEEP and the pay step treat msg.value when the pool currency is the CELO token and when it is address(0)?
leads.why: 88 pools use the CELO token address and 18 use address(0), and the periphery treats the token, which is the native balance itself, as a wrapper. Core was cleared for the two faces. The periphery that ordinary users go through was not read in five cycles.

leads.question: Settle F-024 with the observation named in lead L-263: read what the per transaction observation limits of the X Layer builder filter count, then look for one mined transaction after 10 November 2026 that exceeds a limit. Does one exist?
leads.why: F-024 has been plausible for five cycles on one fact, whether the filter is switched on for the mainnet sequencer. One transaction above the limit shows it is off.

leads.question: Settle F-020 with one fact: does HyperCore require proof of control (a signature, a CoreWriter action or a deployer match) from the EVM address that an AQAv2 treasury designation names before unsigned transfers leave that address? Look for a designation whose named address is a contract that never called CoreWriter, and for the validator vote or action type that created it.
leads.why: F-020 stays plausible on this rule. If no proof is required, the party that can name the address can move tokens out of a contract that cannot sign, which is the operator hazard the finding describes.

leads.question: Settle F-062 with one observation: in a MegaETH block that holds a transaction filling the per block budget for new state, are the transactions after it ordered by arrival or by priority fee, and were later candidates of that block skipped? Use the receipts and the mini block fields of recent blocks.
leads.why: F-062 is plausible because the payload builder is closed and its ordering rule was inferred. The delay it describes exists only if a paying transaction cannot move ahead of the queue.

leads.question: Answer the three open items of lead L-313 by reading src/ and by behaviour tests on a deployed PoolManager. For sync without a lock: which network lets code run between another user's token transfer and that user's settle? For take on an address without code: which addresses change from no code to code at a scheduled fork, and can a pool, a claim or a debt exist under them before it? For the functions without noDelegateCall: call unlock, take, settle, mint and burn through DELEGATECALL from a stub and say what an account that points its EIP-7702 delegation at the PoolManager exposes. Then answer L-314: which lines of the custody path would no test in test/ catch if removed?
leads.why: No unit has read src/ since cycle 3 and these leads were not assigned twice. The first item of L-313 is answered by the cycle 1 items and by the critic's check that the deployed contracts collect fees inside an unlock.

leads.question: Run the behaviour test of lead L-217 on the Unichain predeploy with a caller contract placed by state override: settle with value after sync of a token reverts with NonzeroNativeValue, settle after sync(address(0)) credits msg.value, take reverts while locked, clear accepts only the exact positive delta, mint and burn move the delta and the claim by the same amount, and collectProtocolFees for a synced token reverts.
leads.why: The predeploy has 24,050 bytes against 24,009 elsewhere, and every Unichain result of five cycles describes it. The test takes one sitting and has been skipped four times.

leads.question: For DEAD 0xf0197f10ea542a67914ecc0ec5304dc9df1faf6f on Base: what is the token worth, which pools hold it (read their PoolKey from the Initialize logs through base.gateway.tenderly.co), how much do pools record against the 1,660.03 DEAD the PoolManager holds, and do other tokens on the 21 networks share the selector of claimIdleTokens(address) or the TokensClaimed topic 0xa86305abc2db271df4609aa86a8d044bc11fb36939841bfdad6c1ab2b26e9471?
leads.why: The claim took 14,899.78 DEAD from hookless pools and can repeat on about 18 February 2027. The value and the number of tokens built from the same template decide the severity of the finding.

leads.question: Fill the missing counts in the second finding of theme-unbacked-claims from its work directory (rows, tokens, flagged and confirmed for Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain). Which template produced the tokens that grant the helpers 0xd8e11826e82619bf49c58c05f26c8e00b0b64ea4 and 0xa25c886dced0e8fc0129082bf597381ea073c925 an allowance from the PoolManager through selector 0x73ed6b13, how many live tokens of it still have a PoolManager balance, and what does the implementation behind the PUSD proxy 0xc8fb643d18f1e53698cfda5c8fdf0cdc03c1dbec check in burnFrom?
leads.why: The finding text has eleven empty placeholders, so its size on two networks cannot be judged. The helper selector removed the balance of 30 tokens and live tokens of the template can be listed before they are used.

leads.question: What is TITHE 0x3751b9250a90342e47173bd3a7c7de4f297c060a worth, which pools hold it, does claimFor pay the same amount when the PoolManager holds its full balance of 145,685.74, and do the other Robinhood Chain tokens with the same selector set pay rewards to the PoolManager?
leads.why: 10,002.56 TITHE can be booked by any account today. The measurement was taken after a third of the balance had been moved out for the test, and no price was found.

leads.question: After each Bor release: does 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001010 still return false for transfer without value and true for a zero amount, and did any genesis contract change code? When the Igloo rule set for the C-Chain is published: does it include ACP-209 with the precompile at 0x0200000000000000000000000000000000000006, which takes value for a named account?
leads.why: Polygon forks reach validators as private builds, and Uburu replaced the code at 0x1001. A version of 0x1010 that moves POL without value would turn the dead credit of F-008 into a second working face of the native asset, with the guard at src/PoolManager.sol:356 as the only protection.

leads.question: Check ArbOwnerPublic.getScheduledUpgrade() on Elysium once per cycle (selector 0x81ef944c at 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000006b). When it returns a version and a time, answer L-001 and L-134 on the testnet first: how are ElysiumCoreWriter callbacks delivered, does the predeploy accept value with empty calldata and credit msg.sender, and does it answer balanceOf or transfer?
leads.why: The call returned zeros on 2026-11-23, so nothing can be read today. A callback that the node runs inside a user's call, or a predeploy that books value to the sender, would touch assumptions A1 and A3 on the network with 131,891 pools.
